extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent attorneys/agents and applicants (especially in chemistry/biotechnology prosecution)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for assessing unity of invention, divisional application handling, and special examination and claim-drafting requirements for chemical and biotechnology inventions. Includes criteria for sufficiency of disclosure, claim formats (compound/composition/process/use), and formal/divisional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention — common special technical feature
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity exists between claims that share the same or corresponding 'special technical feature' (the technical feature that constitutes the contribution over the prior art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims are considered to have unity when they have a common special technical feature even if one is a product claim and another a process claim (if process steps are specially adapted to produce the product feature disclosed in the description). Examples: product claim with a specified yield strength and a process claim with steps specially adapted to produce that yield strength — unity exists. Conversely, claims without the same or corresponding special technical feature lack unity (examples given with paint/substance X and electrode arrangement A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity among claims derived from same feature across categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims of different categories (product, process, apparatus, use) have unity when they all share the same special technical feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: fuel burner with tangential fuel inlets: device claims, process claims and apparatus claims that all embody 'tangential fuel inlets' have unity (claims 1,2,4,6). Claims that do not share that feature (e.g., casting procedure or automatic control unit) lack unity with the others.

rubrics_metrics.name: No lack-of-unity objection between a genuine dependent claim and its independent claim
rubrics_metrics.description: A real dependent claim that contains all features of the independent claim shall not be objected for lack of unity with the independent claim, even if the dependent claim adds another invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: dependent claim that narrows temperature range of a claimed process — even if the temperature range itself could be inventive, no unity objection is raised. However, if a claim appears dependent in form but omits features (thus is actually independent), unity must be examined under independent-claim rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when dependent-appearing claim is actually independent
rubrics_metrics.description: If a claim that appears dependent does not contain all features of the independent claim (e.g. replaces feature C with D), it is actually an independent claim and unity should be examined as between independent claims of the same category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert to claims that are dependent in wording but lack essential features; treat such claims as independent for unity assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of lack of novelty/inventive step of an independent claim on unity
rubrics_metrics.description: If an independent claim lacks novelty or inventive step and thus is not patentable, unity among its dependent or parallel independent claims may need re-assessment; remaining claims may be treated as independent for unity purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: display with features A and B (claim 1) and dependent claims with C and D — if claim 1 is unpatentable, claims 2 and 3 may be taken as independent and unity assessed between their special technical features C and D. If C and D are unrelated, there is no unity between them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner invitation to amend or divide when unity lacking
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application contains two or more inventions not forming a single general inventive concept, the examiner shall invite the applicant to restrict claims to one invention or to inventions belonging to a single general inventive concept; applicant may file divisional applications for removed inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner's invitation normally asks the applicant to restrict to e.g. the invention corresponding to claim 1. Filing divisionals for removed inventions is at applicant's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application: circumstances that justify filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Divisional applications may be filed where: (1) original claims contain multiple inventions lacking unity; (2) an added/replacing independent claim during amendment lacks unity with original claims; (3) one independent claim lacks novelty/inventive step and there is no unity among the other claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and explanations are provided for each circumstance. The examiner should invite restriction/amendment and remind applicant of withdrawal consequences; applicant may choose to file a divisional for subject matter removed after amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application text and form requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application must indicate at the beginning of its description the original application from which it is divided and the filing date, application number and title; a copy of the original application must be submitted (and priority documents if priority is claimed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to include the required reference/copies may render the divisional defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application must not extend beyond original disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application shall not go beyond the scope of disclosure contained in the initial (parent) application; otherwise it shall be rejected under Administrative Instruction 28.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the divisional goes beyond the original disclosure, the examiner shall invite amendments; failure to amend or amendments that still go beyond may lead to rejection either for non-compliance with Admin Instruction 28 or Section 3(10)(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims relationship between parent and divisional after division
rubrics_metrics.description: After division, the claims of the parent application and the divisional shall claim protection of different inventions respectively; descriptions may differ (either keep both inventions or only the one relevant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: parent claims invention A and may retain description of A and B or only A; divisional claiming B may retain both or only B in the description. The claims must be for different inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedure on division
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is divided, the divisional and the parent after division are examined according to Administrative Instruction 28; the examiner invites amendments to remedy lack of unity and may reject applications failing to meet requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also reference to Admin Instruction 21: if application does not conform with Section 2(9)(a) the examiner shall invite amendment within time limit and remind applicant of deemed withdrawal if no response; similar approach for divisionals lacking unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability of natural substances vs isolated/extracted products
rubrics_metrics.description: A natural substance found in nature in its natural state is an unpatentable scientific discovery; however, if a substance is isolated or extracted for the first time, is precisely characterized (structure, morphology, parameters) and is industrially exploitable, the substance per se and the process for obtaining it may be patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key is precise characterization and industrial applicability; mere discovery of natural existence is not patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical use exclusion and Harare Protocol exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical-use of a substance for diagnosis or treatment of diseases falls under exclusions (paragraph 3.3.4.1) and generally shall not be granted a patent right; however, use of a substance for manufacturing a medicament may be patentable under the Harare Protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between direct medical treatment/diagnosis uses (excluded) and manufacturing uses for medicaments (possible exception).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient disclosure for chemical product inventions — identification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The description shall describe identification of the chemical product: for compounds, indicate chemical name and structural formula (functional groups, stereochemistry) or molecular formula; provide property parameters (spectra, qualitative/quantitative data) sufficient for a skilled person to identify the compound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For high molecular compounds, also disclose molecular weight and distribution, arrangement of repeating units, crystallinity, density, glass transition etc. If structure cannot fully identify the product, provide property parameters and/or manufacturing process to clearly identify the claimed product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient disclosure for chemical product inventions — preparation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The description shall disclose at least one preparation method for the chemical product, including raw materials, procedures, conditions and specially adapted equipment so that a person skilled in the art can carry it out; examples usually required for compound inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient experimental details; absence of a preparation example for a compound invention is usually insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient disclosure for chemical product inventions — use and technical effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The description must fully disclose the use(s) and/or technical effect(s) of the chemical product. If a skilled person could not predict the stated use/effect from prior art, provide qualitative/quantitative experimental data to convince a skilled person the effect is achievable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For new pharmaceutical compounds/compositions, disclose specific medical use, pharmacological action, effective amount and method of application; supply laboratory/animal/clinical test data when predictability is lacking. Specify measurement methods when different methods yield different results; explain special methods in detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient disclosure for chemical process inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: For chemical process inventions, the description shall disclose raw materials, procedures, processing conditions, and, if necessary, effects of the process on the properties of the product to enable a skilled person to carry out the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also describe the components, properties, manufacturing process or source of raw materials so a skilled person can obtain them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific mode for carrying out chemical inventions (embodiments requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The description generally shall include embodiments and the number of embodiments depends on the extent of generalization in the claims; there must be a sufficient number of embodiments to show how to make and use the invention across the whole claimed scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims are judged on the initial description and claims only; embodiments or data submitted after filing are not considered in sufficiency assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim drafting for compounds
rubrics_metrics.description: A compound claim shall be characterized by the chemical name or the structural/molecular formula, using general nomenclature rather than trade or code names; the structure must be clear and unambiguous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague or ambiguous wording in compound claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim drafting for compositions — open-ended and close-ended modes
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition claims may be presented in open-ended mode ('comprising', 'including', 'containing', 'essentially comprising', etc.) allowing unspecified additional components, or close-ended mode ('consisting of', 'be composed of', 'be balanced with', etc.) excluding other components (except normal impurities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chosen mode must be supported by the description. If nothing else is described in the description, an open-ended formulation is inappropriate. The mode used affects whether subsequent claims with added components are dependent or independent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of components and contents in composition claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention lies in component selection alone and a skilled person can determine contents from prior art/simple experiment, components alone may be defined; if the invention also depends on contents, both components and contents must be defined in the independent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In fields like alloys, necessary components and their contents usually must be defined. Avoid ambiguous terms like 'about' or 'approximately' for content ranges; use numeric expressions (e.g., '0-X', '< X'). Total percentage contents must sum to 100% and content ranges must satisfy min/max constraints described in the guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of diagrams/formulae and qualitative descriptors in composition claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where relations among components are difficult to indicate by words or numbers, a formula or diagram may be used (with explanation in the description). Qualitative descriptions instead of numeric expressions are acceptable if clear and known in the art (e.g., 'catalytic amount').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain any diagram's specific meaning in the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of composition claims (non-defining, function-defining, use-defining)
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition claims can be non-defining (specifying components without limiting to a function), function-defining (specifying properties or functions), or use-defining (specifying intended use); choice depends on disclosed properties and intended application (e.g., most pharmaceutical claims should be use-defining).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If composition has multiple applicable properties/uses, non-defining claim is permitted; if only one property/use is disclosed, use function- or use-defining claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims for chemical products not clearly characterizable by structure/composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a chemical product cannot be clearly characterized by structure or composition alone, it is permitted to characterize the claim by physical/chemical parameter(s) and/or the manufacturing process, provided the parameters/process are clear enough to identify the product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only permitted under circumstances where other features cannot sufficiently characterize the product; parameters must be precise and supported by the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming chemical processes — selectable feature types
rubrics_metrics.description: A chemical process claim may be defined by procedure features (process steps and conditions like temperature, pressure, time, catalysts), substance features (components, structural/formula/property parameters of raw materials or products), or apparatus features (type of apparatus specially adapted or properties/functions of apparatus used).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the type(s) of features depending on subject matter, technical problem, and substance of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use claims in chemistry — nature and claim form
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention relating to the use of a chemical product (based on discovery of a new property) is essentially a process invention and its claim should be a process claim; if product B is invented by making use of product A, the application should be based on product B per se and the claim be a product claim rather than a use claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish carefully whether the invention is in the product or in the application of a product's property; draft claims accordingly (use = process claim; product by use = product claim).
